items.review_rationale: Reviewed Dedekind-cut real model as all rational lower cuts ordered by inclusion, rational embedding by strict lower sets, and resulting real-field axioms after arithmetic and completeness are proved.

references.phrase: real ordered field realized by cuts
set of all rational lower cuts R_D
references.context: Family of qualifying Dedekind cuts, serving as underlying set of the concrete real model.
Injection of rational field into lower cuts by strict lower segment.
Cut-based binary addition and multiplication, requiring separate well-definedness and field-axiom proofs.

references.phrase: ordered-field axioms and completeness as proof obligations
references.disposition: This formulation describes a construction whose arithmetic and least-upper-bound properties must be established; it does not claim those theorems proved.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed a rational lower cut as a proper nonempty downward-closed rational subset with no largest member; retained rational-order scope.

references.context: Set containing some rational but not every rational.
If a belongs to A then every rational q<a must also lie in A.
For every a in A another b in A satisfies a<b.

references.phrase: lower cut excludes whole Q and empty set
references.disposition: Both properness and nonemptiness are explicit, unlike arbitrary downsets.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed rational Cauchy sequence with rational epsilon test for all sufficiently late pairs of indices, without presuming a rational or real limit exists.

references.context: For each rational epsilon>0 exists N with every pair of indices m,n>=N having |a_m-a_n|<epsilon.
Positive integer cutoff after which all comparisons satisfy the epsilon inequality.

references.disposition: Being Cauchy in Q does not imply convergence to a rational number.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed equivalence of two rational Cauchy sequences by eventual epsilon closeness of pointwise difference to zero, preserving all quantifiers and positive-rational epsilon scope.

references.context: For every rational epsilon>0, beyond some common N every index n satisfies |a_n-b_n|<epsilon.
Relation identifying any two Cauchy sequences whose termwise difference tends to zero.

references.disposition: Condition is formulated using only rational arithmetic and needs no previously constructed real field.
